title: Comparison of geometric module stalks normalized on constant sheaves
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] and $\Lambda$ a commutative ring. Let $s:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$ and $t:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\prime\to X$ have the same image point, where $\Omega,\Omega\prime$ are separably closed fields. On the category of $\Lambda$-module sheaves on the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], there exists a natural isomorphism $\beta:(-)_{s}\simeq(-)_{t}$ between the stalk functors [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. For every $\Lambda$-module $M$, the component $\beta_{M_X}$ is identity on $M$ under the canonical identifications of the stalks of the constant sheaf $M_X$ [def-constructible-constant] with $M$. No monomorphism, subsheaf, genericity or finiteness is assumed.

source.place: Tag 04FN (stalk functors and pointed neighbourhoods), combined with Tag 09BH (3), generic submodule paragraph; agent-written separably closed module-valued formulation

proof.text: Let x be the common image. Using the field-spectrum/residue-field description of the geometric points, embed a separable closure K of kappa(x) into both separably closed fields (Mathlib IsSepClosed.lift). Both geometric points factor through Spec K over X.

Precomposition along either factor induces a bijection on pointed etale lifts. A lift into an etale neighbourhood is a residue-field embedding of a finite separable extension of kappa(x). Its image lies in the embedded separable closure K, and thus it factors uniquely through K. These bijections commute with maps of etale neighbourhoods, giving natural isomorphisms of the point fibre functors. This is the separably closed version of the pointed-neighbourhood argument of Stacks Tag 04FN.

Apply the colimit description of geometric stalks to these fibre-functor isomorphisms and compose one comparison with the inverse of the other. Naturality in module sheaves follows from naturality of the colimit coprojections. Each comparison preserves germs of constant sections. The stalk of the constant presheaf is its value, and sheafification does not change stalks. Consequently the composite is identity on the value of every constant module sheaf under the canonical constant-stalk isomorphisms.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_geometricStalkComparison_constant
    {X : Scheme.{u}} {Λ : Type (u + 1)} [CommRing Λ]
    [Limits.PreservesFilteredColimitsOfSize.{u, u} (CategoryTheory.forget (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ))]
    {Ω Ω' : Type u} [Field Ω] [IsSepClosed Ω] [Field Ω'] [IsSepClosed Ω']
    (s : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ X) (t : Spec (.of Ω') ⟶ X)
    (h : s (IsLocalRing.closedPoint Ω) = t (IsLocalRing.closedPoint Ω')) :
    ∃ β : (pointSmallEtale s).sheafFiber (A := ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) ≅
        (pointSmallEtale t).sheafFiber,
      ∀ M : ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ,
        β.hom.app ((constantSheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ)).obj M) ≫
          ((pointSmallEtale t).sheafFiberConstantSheafIso M).hom =
          ((pointSmallEtale s).sheafFiberConstantSheafIso M).hom
